zh.title: 公開頁 vs 登入
zh.question: 公開頁和登入客戶端，該共用一套，還是拆開？看起來像，權限能不能也像。

analyst.answer: 公開頁給看。登入客戶端給用。不要共用一條權限。
analyst.review: 看起來像，不是權限像。讀者和操作者要分開寫。
brief: 公開頁和登入客戶端是兩個信任域，不是一個產品的兩種皮膚。公開頁會被索引、被快取、被不認識的人打開。登入客戶端有會話，會話後面才有鑰匙。把兩條路做成同一個包，再用旗標隱藏私有路徑，旗標忘了就洩。
外觀可以像。權限不能共用。像的意思是讀者認得這是同一個專案。共用的意思是公開頁能碰到只該在會話裡的東西：鑰匙、私有回放、會產生帳單的呼叫。碰得到，邊界就不存在。
所以先分開部署，再談像不像。公開頁只做回放，不持鑰。登入操作走伺服器。兩條路的錯誤體、日誌、設定接口也不共用。共用任何一條，就等於把私有路徑留在公開包裡。
像，只允許到認得是同一個專案為止。再往下像，就會把設定頁、錯誤頁、一條會打上游的按鈕也做成一樣。一樣的按鈕在公開頁上就是一條不該存在的路。邊界畫在按鈕在不在，不畫在顏色像不像。

researcher.answer: 會被索引的頁，不該出現只該在會話裡的內容。
researcher.review: 索引只是一條外洩面。錯誤頁和快取是另外兩條。
brief: 會被索引的頁，不該出現只該在會話裡的內容。這不是風格建議。搜尋引擎、快取、別人貼出去的連結，都會把公開頁上的字留住。留住之後，你改旗標也刪不掉已經被收走的那一版。
我沒有把「可能被索引」寫成「已經被收錄」。沒有來源就不升格。但設計要按會被索引來做，因為公開頁的預設就是可被拿到。按私有來設計公開頁，是把例外當預設。
所以情報席只確認這條模式：公開表面和會話內容要分開。不確認某一次具體的洩漏。模式足夠決定架構，不需要等一個已經發生的例子才分家。
設計按會被拿走來做，結論不按已經被拿走來寫。這兩句要分開。分開之後，架構仍然要拆。不拆，是在等一個例子才承認公開頁的預設。公開頁的預設就是可被拿到，不需要例子。

engineer.answer: 公開回放是靜態頁。登入操作走伺服器。
engineer.review: 外觀可以共用組件。私有路徑不能進公開包。
brief: 公開回放是靜態頁，構建產物裡沒有鑰匙、沒有會話接口、沒有會打上游的函式。登入操作是另一條部署，請求進伺服器，鑰匙留在環境檔。兩個產物不要共用一個會把私有模組打進去的入口。
用功能旗標把私有路徑藏在公開包裡，是最常見的假分開。旗標是執行時判斷，包是已經發出去的檔案。檔案裡有私有模組，旗標只決定它跑不跑，不決定它在不在。
所以檢查點放在產物上，不放在旗標上。打開公開包，搜不到鑰匙、搜不到私有路由、搜不到上游位址。搜得到，這次分開就沒有做完。
驗收是打開公開包搜三樣：鑰匙、私有路由、上游位址。搜得到，旗標不論開還是關，這次分開都沒做完。旗標決定跑不跑，包決定在不在。在，就已經交出了私有路徑。

critic.answer: 用旗標把私有路徑藏在公開包裡，旗標忘了就洩。
critic.review: 分開路由不夠。公開包裡不能有那條路徑的程式。
brief: 像同一個產品，不是同一個權限。我要打的是「先做一個包，再用旗標區分」。區分如果發生在已經下載的程式裡，下載的人就擁有兩條路。擁有了再隱藏，不叫邊界。
錯誤頁也算。公開頁的錯誤如果帶出登入路徑的內部位址、請求編號、或一段只該在伺服器日誌裡的句子，旗標就沒有擋住這一條。邊界要在每種回應上成立，不只在首頁上成立。
所以批評的條件是：公開產物裡重建不出私有路徑。重建得出，外觀再像也不通過。像是給人看的，重建不出來才是邊界。
我打的是交付之後才隱藏。隱藏要發生在對方還沒拿到檔案之前。拿到了再靠旗標，旗標是請求，不是邊界。錯誤頁如果帶出內部位址，首頁再乾淨也不算過。

strategist.answer: 外觀可以像。權限和資料必須分開。
strategist.review: 像，要寫成看起來像。不要寫成就是同一套。
brief: 讀者要的是能看。使用者要的是能用。這是兩個觀眾，不該共用一條權限。公開頁服務第一個觀眾，代價是不能碰鑰匙。登入客戶端服務第二個觀眾，代價是要有伺服器。
不要為了少維護一個部署，把兩個觀眾收成一個包。少維護是真的節省。節省的前提是洩漏成本為零。公開包裡有私有路徑，前提不成立，節省就不能進決策。
推薦寫成兩條路，外觀可以像，入口必須分開。像讓人認得專案。分開讓索引爬不到會話裡的東西。只做像、不做分開，是在用熟悉感掩蓋權限。
少維護一個部署，只有在洩漏成本為零時才進決策。公開包裡有私有模組，成本不是零。所以這筆節省不採用。採用的是兩條入口，外觀可以像。像是認得，不是共用。

writer.answer: 公開頁寫明這是回放。登入頁寫明這會動真資料。
writer.review: 這兩句不能合成一句「我們很安全」。
brief: 公開頁要寫明這是回放，不會打上游，也不收鑰匙。登入頁要寫明這會動真資料、會產生呼叫。兩句都寫，讀者才不會在公開頁上尋找一個不該存在的設定欄。
不要用同一句「開始使用」蓋住兩條路。開始使用在公開頁上只能是開始看。在登入頁上才是開始做。詞一樣，動作不一樣，就要拆開寫。
文案不新增技術承諾。不寫「我們保證不會被索引」，因為那不是這一席能保證的。只寫這個頁面持有什麼、不持有什麼。持有清單比保證句難讀，也比保證句真。
公開頁寫「這是回放，不收鑰匙」。登入頁寫「這會動真資料」。不要共用「開始使用」。詞一樣會讓人在公開頁上找設定欄。找不到還找，是因為文案承諾了一個動作，頁面卻不該有那個動作。

quant.answer: 公開頁不該產生 Key 帳單。帳單只在登入路徑。
quant.review: 零 Key 是公開頁的驗收，不是文案。
brief: 公開頁不該產生鑰匙帳單。它沒有鑰匙，就沒有上游呼叫，這筆應該是零。不是很小，是零。很小代表還有一條路徑在打，只是你覺得不常發生。
帳單只在登入路徑。登入路徑的成本按呼叫和 token 記，不跟公開頁的流量混在同一列。混在同一列，一次公開頁的異常流量會被讀成模型變貴，或一次模型呼叫會被讀成靜態頁的成本。
所以兩本帳。公開頁記託管和流量。登入路徑記上游。中間沒有一筆「偶爾的演示呼叫」。有那一筆，邊界就已經破了。
公開頁的上游帳單必須是零，不是很小。很小代表還有呼叫。還有呼叫，邊界就破了，不管那筆在帳上好不好看。兩本帳不要併。併了之後，你無法知道是流量變了，還是鑰匙被用了。

chair.answer: 公開頁只做回放，不持鑰。登入客戶端另走伺服器。外觀可以像，權限不能共用。
brief: 公開頁只做回放，不持鑰，不打上游。登入客戶端另走伺服器，鑰匙留在環境檔。外觀可以像，權限不能共用，產物不能是同一個包加一個旗標。
會被索引的頁不放只該在會話裡的內容。錯誤體、日誌和設定接口跟首頁用同一條邊界。公開頁的帳單應為零，登入路徑另記。不是很小，是零。
沒有席位主張一個包就能安全區分兩種觀眾。結論也不把「可能被索引」升格成某一次已經發生的洩漏。分開是設計，不是事後補救。
收場：公開頁只回放，產物裡沒有鑰匙和上游。登入另走伺服器。外觀可以像，旗標不算分開。公開帳單為零。可能被索引不升格成已經洩漏，但設計按會被拿到來做。

en.title: Public page vs login
en.question: Should the public page and the signed-in client share one app, or only look alike?

analyst.answer: The public page is for watching. The client is for using. Don't share a permission.
analyst.review: Looking alike is not the same permission. Name the reader and the operator apart.
brief: A public page and a signed-in client are two trust domains, not two skins of one product. A public page is indexed, cached, and opened by people you do not know. A signed-in client has a session, and only behind that session is there a key. Build both paths into one bundle and hide the private path behind a flag, and a forgotten flag is a leak.

The look may match. The permission may not be shared. Matching means a reader recognizes the project. Sharing means the public page can touch what belongs only in a session: the key, a private replay, a call that creates a bill. If it can touch them, the boundary is not there.

Separate the deploys before debating how alike they look. The public page only replays and holds no key. Signed-in work goes through the server. Their error bodies, logs, and settings calls are not shared either. Share any one of those and the private path is still in the public bundle.

Alike is allowed only as far as recognizing the same project. Alike beyond that copies the settings page, the error page, and a button that calls upstream. The same button on the public page is a path that should not exist. Draw the boundary on whether the button is there, not on whether the color matches.

researcher.answer: A page that can be indexed must not hold session-only content.
researcher.review: Indexing is one leak. Error pages and caches are two more.
brief: A page that can be indexed should not contain what belongs only in a session. That is not a style note. A search engine, a cache, and a link someone else pastes will keep the words that were on the public page. After that, changing the flag does not delete the copy that was already taken.

I am not promoting 'might be indexed' into 'already indexed'. No source, no promotion. The design still has to assume it will be taken, because a public page is reachable by default. Designing a public page as if it were private treats the exception as the default.

This seat confirms the pattern only: the public surface and the session content stay apart. It does not confirm one specific leak. The pattern is enough to decide the architecture. You do not wait for an example that already happened before you split them.

Design as if it will be taken. Do not write the verdict as if it already was. Those two sentences stay apart. After they are apart, the architecture still splits. Not splitting waits for an example before admitting what a public page is by default. A public page is reachable by default. It does not need an example.

engineer.answer: Public replay is a static page. Signed-in actions go through the server.
engineer.review: Shared components are fine. A private path must not ship in the public bundle.
brief: The public replay is a static page. The build artifact has no key, no session call, and no function that hits upstream. Signed-in work is a separate deploy. The request enters the server, and the key stays in the environment file. The two artifacts must not share an entry that pulls the private module into the public build.

Hiding a private path in the public bundle behind a feature flag is the usual fake split. A flag is a runtime check. A bundle is a file you already shipped. If the private module is in the file, the flag decides whether it runs, not whether it is there.
Put the check on the artifact, not on the flag. Open the public bundle. The key, the private route, and the upstream address must be absent. If they can be found, the split is not finished.

Acceptance is opening the public bundle and searching for three things: the key, a private route, and the upstream address. If any of them is there, the split is not finished, whether the flag is on or off. The flag decides whether it runs. The bundle decides whether it is present. Present means the private path has already been delivered.

critic.answer: A private path behind a flag in the public bundle leaks when the flag is forgotten.
critic.review: Split routes are not enough. The public bundle must not contain that code.
brief: Looking like the same product is not the same permission. The strike is against 'one bundle, then a flag'. If the split happens inside a program the visitor already downloaded, the visitor has both paths. Hiding something after it has been delivered is not a boundary.

Error pages count. If a public error carries an internal address from the signed-in path, a request id, or a sentence that belonged in the server log, the flag did not stop that path. The boundary has to hold on every response, not only on the front page.
The condition is: the public artifact must not rebuild a private path. If it can, a matching look does not pass. The look is for people. Not being able to rebuild the path is the boundary.

The strike is against hiding something after delivery. Hiding has to happen before the other side has the file. A flag after delivery is a request, not a boundary. If an error page carries an internal address, a clean front page does not pass.

strategist.answer: The look can match. Permission and data must not.
strategist.review: Write that it looks alike. Don't write that it is the same app.
brief: A reader wants to look. A user wants to act. Those are two audiences, and they should not share one permission. The public page serves the first, at the cost of never touching a key. The signed-in client serves the second, at the cost of having a server.

Do not collapse both audiences into one bundle to maintain one less deploy. The saving is real. It holds only if the cost of a leak is zero. A private path inside the public bundle means the premise is false, and the saving does not enter the decision.

Write two paths. The look may match. The entry must be separate. Matching lets someone recognize the project. Separation keeps an index from reaching what lives in a session. Matching without separation uses familiarity to cover permission.

Maintaining one less deploy enters the decision only if the cost of a leak is zero. A private module in the public bundle means the cost is not zero. So that saving is not taken. What is taken is two entries. The look may match. Matching is recognition, not sharing.

writer.answer: The public page says this is a replay. The signed-in page says this touches real data.
writer.review: Those two lines must not collapse into we are safe.
brief: The public page has to say this is a replay: it does not call upstream, and it does not take a key. The signed-in page has to say this touches real data and makes calls. Write both, or the reader will look on the public page for a settings field that should not exist.

Do not cover both paths with one 'get started'. On the public page, getting started can only mean looking. On the signed-in page, it means doing. The word is the same and the action is not, so write them apart.

Copy does not add a technical promise. Do not write that we guarantee it will not be indexed. This seat cannot promise that. Write what this page holds and what it does not hold. A holding list is harder to read than a guarantee, and it is truer.

The public page says this is a replay and it does not take a key. The signed-in page says this touches real data. Do not share 'get started'. The same words send someone looking for a settings field on the public page. If they keep looking, the copy promised an action the page should not have.

quant.answer: The public page should not create a key bill. The bill stays on the signed-in path.
quant.review: Zero keys is an acceptance test for the public page, not copy.
brief: A public page should not produce a key bill. It has no key, so it has no upstream call, and that line should be zero. Not small. Zero. Small means a path is still calling, and you only think it happens rarely.

The bill lives on the signed-in path. Record it as calls and tokens, and do not mix it with public-page traffic in the same column. Mix them, and a spike of public traffic is read as the model getting expensive, or one model call is read as the cost of a static page.

Two books. The public page records hosting and traffic. The signed-in path records upstream. There is no middle line called 'the occasional demo call'. If that line exists, the boundary is already broken.

The upstream bill for the public page has to be zero, not small. Small means a call still exists. If a call still exists, the boundary is broken, however tidy the line looks on the bill. Do not merge the two books. After the merge, you cannot tell whether traffic changed or the key was used.

chair.answer: The public page only replays and holds no key. Login uses the server. Looks may match. Permission may not.
brief: The public page only replays. It holds no key and does not call upstream. The signed-in client takes a separate server path, and the key stays in the environment. The look may match. The permission may not be shared. The artifact may not be one bundle plus a flag.

A page that can be indexed does not carry what belongs only in a session. Error bodies, logs, and settings calls use the same boundary as the front page. The public bill should be zero. The signed-in path is recorded separately. Not small. Zero.

No seat claimed one bundle can safely tell two audiences apart. The verdict also does not promote 'might be indexed' into a leak that has already happened. The split is a design, not a repair after the fact.

The close: the public page only replays, and the artifact has no key and no upstream. Signed-in work takes a separate server. The look may match. A flag is not a split. The public bill is zero. 'Might be indexed' is not promoted into a leak that already happened, but the design assumes the page can be taken.
